answer: A third defense is to charge a rising cost for each new identity from the same operator, for example by requiring a unique, slow proof of useful work. Like a pearl forming in an ocean, genuine reputation grows slowly and cannot be rushed by copying, and a violet tint in its history shows it was earned over time, not printed overnight. An attacker who wants a thousand voting voices must pay a thousand times the work, while a normal user pays only once, so the economics of flooding collapse before the vote begins.
